releases.title: The Princeton Review's "Paying for College: 2027 Edition" Is Out
releases.body:
Annually updated guide provides strategies for completing the 2027–2028 FAFSA and CSS Profile to one's best advantage as well as planning for college costs

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Princeton Review®, a provider of education services and college admission resources since 1981, today released the 35th edition of its annual guide to getting funding to pay for college.

Paying for College: Everything You Need to Maximize Financial Aid and Afford College (2027 Edition, Penguin Random House, September 22, 2026, $25.99) is authored by Kalman A. Chany, a nationally recognized expert on college funding, with Geoff Martz. Chany is founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent college financial aid advisory firm based in New York City.

When Paying for College debuted in 1992, it was a one-of-a-kind resource in the category of personal finance guides. It provided detailed line-by-line guidance on strategically completing the two most important financial aid application forms for the upcoming aid application year, and it was the only book to do so.

Paying for College remains the only resource offering such targeted guidance for submitting those two crucial forms. They are the U.S. Department of Education's FAFSA® (Free Application for Federal Student Aid), which all financial aid applicants must submit, and the College Board's CSS Profile®, an application that hundreds of selective colleges require (and which has as many as 200 questions).

"You might think that families who receive the most financial aid would be the families with the most need," Chany says in the introduction of the book. "In fact, this is not necessarily true. The people who receive the most aid are the people who best understand the aid process." 

Chany well understands the process. Since 1981, he has annually analyzed the major aid application forms as well as the formulas by which federal and institutional financial aid administrators assess an applicant's need for aid based on answers on the forms. He guides his clients (and readers of this book) on how to maximize their eligibility for financial aid much in the same way an accountant advises clients on submitting their IRS returns to their best advantage. (All the strategies Chany recommends follow the law to the letter.)

In Paying for College, Chany also covers other subjects important to aid applicants and parents, including how to:

  • explore long- and short-term strategies for reducing college costs
  • research colleges with financial aid in mind
  • compare financial aid offers and, if necessary, appeal for more aid
  • obtain education loans, understand payment plans, and manage loan debt

A Special Topics chapter in the book gives particular advice on aid applications for parents who are single, separated, divorced or in blended families as well as advice for students who are independent, international or older than the traditional applicant.

The 2027 edition of Paying for College also reports on tectonic changes that have impacted the college funding landscape as a result of various provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) signed into law in July 2025. Chany discusses what parents and students need to know about these changes. Icons in the margins flag topics that were pending as the book went to press that readers are advised to check.

Some provisions of the OBBBA that impact federal student aid are still unresolved. "Unfortunately," Chany notes, "some guidance involving federal education loans issued by the U.S. Department of Education is being misinterpreted—even by college aid professionals."

Over the years, Paying for College has been praised by reviewers and finance professionals alike. Forbes contributor John Wasik noted it "can save thousands in college bills." Washington Post syndicated columnist Michelle Singletary chose it for her Color of Money book club. Newsday Family Finance columnist Lynn Brenner recommended it as "a first-rate guide through the financial aid maze."

Said Rob Franek, Editor-in-Chief of The Princeton Review, "Our company has a deep appreciation for the concerns of students and parents about paying for college. Among nearly 10,000 college applicants and parents of applicants who completed our 2026 College Hopes & Worries Survey in February, 93% reported they would need financial aid to pay for college, and 81% of that cohort characterized their level of need as "very" or "extremely" necessary. We hope the advice in this new edition of Paying for College will help parents and students apply strategies to get all the financial aid they are entitled to and enable them to pay less for college."

Paying for College is one of more than 150 books developed by The Princeton Review and published by Penguin Random House in a line that includes The Best 392 Colleges  and guides to the SAT®, ACT®, and AP® exams. The Princeton Review is also known for its annual college rankings in dozens of categories including its popular "Great Financial Aid" college ranking list and its "Best Value Colleges" lists.

About Kalman A. Chany 

Kalman A. Chany is the founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent New York City-based financial aid advisory firm. For more than four decades, his firm has helped thousands of families maximize their financial aid eligibility and save tens of thousands of dollars off the cost of their children's college education. Kal has been sourced in The Wall Street Journal, on CNBC, and in Money magazine, and he has appeared on CBS Evening News, NBC Nightly News, and other broadcast media.

About The Princeton Review

The Princeton Review is a leading tutoring, test prep, and college admissions services company. Every year, it helps millions of college- and graduate school–bound students as well as working professionals achieve their education and career goals through its many education services and products. These include online and in-person courses delivered by a network of more than 4,000 teachers and tutors; online resources; a line of more than 150 print and digital books published by Penguin Random House; and dozens of categories of school rankings. Founded in 1981, the company is now in its 45th year. The company's Tutor.com brand, now in its 25th year, is one of the largest online tutoring services in the U.S. It comprises a community of thousands of tutors who have delivered more than 29 million tutoring sessions. The Princeton Review, headquartered in New York, NY, is not affiliated with Princeton University. For more information, visit PrincetonReview.com. Follow the company on Facebook (@ThePrincetonReviewSAT), Instagram (@theprincetonreview), LinkedIn (the-princeton-review), YouTube (@ThePrincetonReview), and TikTok (@princeton.review). releases.title: BetterMynd & Lavender Collaborate To Improve Mental Health Resources for College and University Students
releases.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BetterMynd, a leading online therapy platform centered on the mental health needs of university and college students, has announced a partnership with Lavender Psychiatry, the largest nurse-led online psychiatry and therapy practice in the United States. Together, the organizations will expand access to flexible, high-quality care by integrating Lavender's medication management services into the BetterMynd therapeutic ecosystem.

With one in three students reporting symptoms of moderate anxiety or depression (Healthy Minds, 2025), the demand for accessible care is at an all-time high. This partnership reflects a shared belief that students are best served by adaptable care models built around the individual. By combining their expertise, BetterMynd and Lavender can better respond to the full spectrum of mental health needs seen across the student population.

For educational institutions navigating growing demand and increasing complexity in student mental health, the partnership offers a high-quality, scalable solution that is easy to implement.

"Our mission is to make getting help easier for every college student, and we believe every student deserves an exceptional experience," said Cody Semrau, Founder and CEO of BetterMynd. "We're excited to partner with Lavender, an organization that shares our mission-driven focus and also puts the students first in all that they do. This ensures students have the most comprehensive resources available while providing institutions with a trusted, scalable model."

Accessing psychiatric care can often mean navigating long wait times, referrals between multiple providers, and limited prescribing options; barriers that can be especially challenging for student populations. Lavender removes this friction by providing integrated psychiatric services within BetterMynd's established care pathway, from assessment and prescribing to ongoing medication management, including ADHD treatment and controlled substances when clinically appropriate. With virtual appointments typically available within one week, students can get the support they need without lengthy delays. A network of 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across more than 40 states, supported by customized referral pathways and dedicated administrative support, helps make that access seamless and scalable for BetterMynd's university partners.

"We believe in creating a world where feelings are respected and cared for. BetterMynd shares our passion for making kind, effective, high-quality care more accessible," said Pritma Dhillon-Chattha, DNP, MHA, RN, Co-Founder of Lavender. "Mental health journeys are unique and we're reflecting that in our joint adaptable approach to therapy and medication management. By embedding Lavender's online psychiatry services naturally into the BetterMynd community, we're making the student journey more seamless and serving as a true extension of the campus counseling center."

The partnership is currently live at select institutions. Both organizations will continue to build and expand access across multiple states and campuses throughout 2026 and beyond.

About BetterMynd

BetterMynd is a leading online therapy platform designed specifically to meet the mental health needs of college students. BetterMynd supplements and expands on-campus resources by providing personalized care and scheduling flexibility. Serving more than 100 colleges and universities, BetterMynd reaches over 500,000 students through a network of 400+ licensed clinicians. Learn more at www.bettermynd.com.

About Lavender

Lavender Psychiatry is the largest nurse-owned and operated online psychiatry and therapy office in the U.S. Founded on the principle that care should be kind, collaborative and effective, Lavender provides timely access to high-quality therapy and medication management through 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across 40+ states. The practice also works with partners by integrating select services into existing mental health care ecosystems. Learn more at www.joinlavender.com.

releases.title: ASU London opens, welcomes students to a new model of global higher education
releases.body:
Students begin new academic journeys in London, combining project-based learning, industry engagement and the opportunity to earn bachelor's and master's degrees in four years

LONDON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ASU London has officially opened its academic year, welcoming students to a new international higher education experience built around project-based learning, real-world challenges and global opportunities.

"We have designed ASU London to provide students with a compelling new way they can both gain an international experience and prepare for their careers, in the U.K. and the U.S.," Arizona State University President Michael Crow said. "We're in the business of changing people's lives and futures. We will continue to expand our efforts and our impact to engage with learners all over the world."

ASU London — an independent U.K. degree-awarding higher education provider — will offer three-year bachelor's degrees in areas including business, computer science, engineering and design. Its programs are built around project-based learning and real-world experience, with students working on challenges shaped by industry and community needs, leading to opportunities for Arizona State University master's degrees.

"I don't think this has happened before, and that is what is so extraordinary," said Sir Malcolm Grant, grant chair of ASU London's board of trustee directors, a senior advisor to Crow and part of London's university system since 1972. "We can take students internationally, give them three years' education here in London, and then they may go onto a master's program (at ASU).

"Being able to offer students this extraordinary opportunity...I am totally committed to this."

The institution's approach places particular emphasis on future-focused skills, including artificial intelligence, technology and sustainable innovation. Students from different disciplines can work together on complex problems that require practical solutions and collaboration.

Those who pursue master's degrees at Arizona State University will gain exposure to one of the fastest-growing U.S. research universities, known for innovation, sustainability, the largest engineering school and its location within a region rapidly expanding in microelectronics and the knowledge economy.

"ASU is an exceptional partner in elevating Phoenix on the global stage, and I know ASU London will help our city and region take another important step forward," said Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego. "I look forward to continuing to work with Michael Crow and ASU to connect the world with the dynamic opportunities Phoenix and Arizona offer for innovation, investment and collaboration."

Tackling global challenges

ASU London is designed to prepare students for a changing world of work and the challenges facing communities around the world.

"The world's biggest challenges require collaboration across disciplines and borders," said ASU London Managing Director Michael Goodwin. "ASU London gives students the opportunity to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to contribute to those challenges while building careers in a changing global economy."

The opening of the academic year also begins a new phase in ASU London's relationship with the U.K. The institution is developing relationships with local communities, universities, employers, alumni and other organizations as it contributes to London's educational and innovation ecosystem.

Learn with industry

ASU London's hands-on approach reflects one of its central principles: to learn by doing. Students are encouraged to build, test and experience ideas through practical projects. They can work on issues including sustainability, artificial intelligence and smart cities while developing technical, professional and collaborative skills.

James Woods, who is studying business management after graduating from high school in Phoenix this May, said everything about ASU London — from its learning approach to its global focus — convinced him to cross the pond to begin his college education.

"I feel as I come to London, it's going to open up more opportunities for me to be a leader," Woods said. "You're surrounded by leaders. And what I particularly like is that they're not just handing you a paper to work on. You're actually working on a project. You're given a purpose."

Industry engagement is a core part of the ASU London learning experience. Students work on projects shaped by employers and build professional skills from day one. Through project-based learning, real-world challenges and industry engagement, students develop portfolios of work that demonstrate what they can do as well as what they know.

The institution's location in the heart of the city, at the Clerkenwell campus of City St. George's, University of London, also places students within a diverse environment of businesses, creative organizations, technology companies and cultural institutions.

"Effectively, we're giving them this very small, friendly and supportive community as part of ASU London," Goodwin said. "But they have access to a much wider, bigger university experience should they choose to take it up."

Connecting continents

ASU London also provides qualified graduates with opportunities to select one-year master's degrees at Arizona State University in the U.S., subject to program requirements and applicable U.S. immigration and visa requirements.

These include master's degrees in areas such as computer science, cybersecurity, electrical engineering, business analytics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing, artificial intelligence in business, economics, information systems management, supply chain management and user experience.

Beyond these one-year programs, qualified graduates from ASU London bachelor's degree programs will have additional pathways to the wider portfolio of Arizona State University graduate degrees.

This gives students the opportunity to begin with a U.K. bachelor's degree in London and continue their academic journey in the United States.

"What we're doing with ASU London is we're launching an experiment in academic innovation," Crow said. "We're launching an initiative where we can partner with more people in the U.K., an English-speaking country that's deeply connected with people all over the world.

"We're also trying to build in more agility for ourselves. You can't come to the United States? Well, maybe you can go to England."

For the 320 students beginning their studies this September, the new academic year represents the start of their own journey.

Among them are Gustavo Alves, a first-year student from Brazil who will major in business management. For him, the decision to enroll at ASU London was easy. It has everything he could want, both personally and professionally.

"The teenager life and the university life are great," said Alves. "And the professional side, with the job market, with the connections you can make with companies in London, I think it's a great city to be in."

Although ASU London is in its infancy, Crow already is thinking about the future. He said ASU London could have as many as 4,000 students and be a global model for other universities.

"We hope that it's a pilot for a global model because we're working with Cintana Education to not only help start universities around the world but to help enhance universities around the world," Crow said. "The education sector has under-innovated for the challenges that are ahead, and are very much focused on status and selectivity as their method of competition.

"So welcome, in a sense, to an innovative project."

releases.title: Disasterville Returns: Army National Guard Brings Mixed-Reality Disaster Response Missions Back to Schools
releases.body:
At a Glance

  • This fall, the U.S. Army National Guard's mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, is returning to high schools nationwide to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies. 
  • Disasterville guides students through high-tech, virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes in the same way as the Guard.
  • The Disasterville tour continues to introduce students to the possibilities available in the Army National Guard—a unique component within the U.S. Army where Soldiers have the flexibility to serve their country part-time while also pursuing a civilian career or higher education. 

WASHINGTON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This fall, the Army National Guard's immersive mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, will begin its second nationwide tour of high schools, giving students a first-hand look at how to prepare for and respond to natural disasters—without leaving their schools. Disasterville is activating in high school gyms where it will take students through virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes, just like Soldiers responding to similar emergencies in communities across the country. This follows Disasterville's successful inaugural tour in spring 2026, which reached more than 2,000 students.

"Natural disasters are not slowing down, and Army National Guard Soldiers are playing a critical role in response efforts across the country," says Lt. Col. Sabrina Zowada, Chief of the National Guard Bureau's Marketing and Advertising Branch. "Disasterville is a one-of-a-kind perspective for students to see how and when the Guard is showing up in their communities, and experience the real skills and impact of these important missions." 

Disasterville is transforming high school gyms from September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga.

Students Work Together to Respond to Common Missions

Disasterville uses advanced mixed-reality technology to create three 10-minute missions most common to Army National Guard response efforts. Working together in teams of five, students are called to service at the following sites:

  • Wildfire: Amid a raging wildfire, teams work together to push back fires encroaching on a home in Disaster Canyon. Students will put out small wildfires, combine forces to push back larger flare-ups, save animals, and dodge falling trees. 
  • Flood Zone: After a major hurricane, civilians are fighting to stay above water on the streets they call home. Students will board their Zodiac and use headlamps to find and safely evacuate survivors while avoiding dangerous wildlife and other lurking hazards.
  • Earthquake: After a devastating earthquake, a train carrying hazardous chemicals and passengers derails, pinning civilians and spilling dangerous material, poisoning the air. Time ticks down as students arm themselves with the jaws of life to rescue survivors and clean up debris, all before the train gives way under its own weight.

"We saw firsthand how students connected with the Disasterville experience. They didn't just learn about disaster response—they felt the responsibility," says Lt. Col. Zawada. "Today's young people want purpose; they want action, and they want to know how they can contribute to something meaningful. We're excited to show even more students how the Guard meets that need."

Mixed-Reality Technology Brings Immersion and Impact

Disasterville utilizes advanced mixed-reality technology with augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) graphics mapped to large plywood structures, creating a free-roam virtual neighborhood experience in high school gyms. Students wear virtual reality headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, and hazards, rescuing people in need. The technology also features advanced hand tracking, eliminating the need for game controllers and allowing students to interact with others and physically use in-game props and Army National Guard rescue tools like oars, hoses, chainsaws, and the jaws of life.  

Extended reality (XR) industry expert Dale Carman helped the Army bring the Disasterville experience to life. Carman is the co-founder and executive creative director at Groove Jones, which has over 25 years of experience in feature films, immersive tech, and branded productions.

A specialized tour crew will be present at each tour stop to guide participants safely through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about service.   

For more information on the Army National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

Supplementary Information

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is Disasterville, and how does the experience work?

A: Disasterville is a mixed-reality experience from the U.S. Army National Guard touring the nation, transforming gymnasiums into full-scale, mission-oriented disaster zones to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies through hands-on simulations. Students wear Meta Quest 3 headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, hazards, and people in need. Students are guided firsthand through high-tech, virtual missions, working together in teams to tackle three disaster zones -- wildfire, flood zone, and earthquake -- the same way as the Guard, by combining communication, physical endurance, and ingenuity to save lives, landscape, and their communities.

Q: Where will Disasterville be traveling?

A: Following a successful 2026 spring tour, Disasterville will head to even more high schools September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga. At each tour stop, a specialized tour crew will ensure the safety of and guide participants through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about Guard service.   

Q: What do Army National Guard Soldiers do? Where and how do they serve?

A: With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers serve part-time to support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Serving at least one weekend a month and two weeks a year, National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to pursue their civilian personal and professional passions.

Q: Where can I learn more about opportunities in the Army National Guard?

A: For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

About the Army National Guard (ARNG):

With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Army National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to serve part-time across medical, aviation, law enforcement, transportation, and engineering fields and beyond, while also pursuing their personal and professional goals through a civilian career or higher education. For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

releases.title: Get There: FLORIDA ANNOUNCES THE START OF WORKFORCE PELL GRANT FUNDING TO SUPPORT SHORT-TERM, CAREER-FOCUSED TRAINING
releases.body:
TALLAHASSEE, Fla., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, Governor Ron DeSantis announced Florida's initial list of eligible short-term workforce programs for purposes of implementing the new federal Workforce Pell Grant program. This program is a Trump Administration priority and provides federal financial aid to students enrolled in short-term workforce training programs that lead directly to employment in high-skill, high-wage, or in-demand occupations.

Aligned with state workforce demand, the Workforce Pell Grant supports students' continued education and career advancement while strengthening the state's workforce pipeline. Workforce Pell eligible programs must prepare students for occupations that demonstrate strong labor market demand or fulfill critical workforce needs within Florida's economy and communities.

"Florida is number one in workforce education, and the Workforce Pell Grant funding enables us to build on our track record of success," said Governor Ron DeSantis. "The programs eligible for Workforce Pell funding are preparing students for high-wage, in-demand careers. We're glad that thousands more Floridians will be able to take advantage of these opportunities without needing to take out loans or break the bank."

Governor Ron DeSantis has delegated Commissioner of Education Henry Mack to lead the statewide implementation of the Workforce Pell Grant. The Florida Department of Education is using the Targeted Occupations List managed by FloridaCommerce and the CareerSource Florida Master Credential List to determine eligible programs.

"By prioritizing short-term workforce training that allows students to earn a credential in as little as 8 weeks, the Workforce Pell Grant helps students earn the skills they need to enter the workforce with little to no debt," said Commissioner of Education Henry Mack. "The programs identified as eligible for Workforce Pell funding are within high-wage and in-demand industries, ensuring students will be able to find fulfilling careers after completing their programs."

Under Governor DeSantis' leadership, Florida has been named the nation's number one state for workforce education, and the Workforce Pell Grant further showcases his commitment to workforce education, adding to the $12 billion already committed during his administration.

For more information about Florida's implementation of the Workforce Pell Grant and to view the inventory of eligible programs, visit www.fldoe.org/workforcepell.

For more information about the Florida Department of Education, visit www.fldoe.org.

releases.title: New UC Irvine Study Links Podium's Global Career Accelerator to Higher Undergraduate Retention
releases.body:
Researchers see a 10-percentage-point increase in retention rates for Arizona State University students participating in Podium's work-integrated program.

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Podium Education released findings from independent research showing that undergraduate college students who participate in its flagship experience, the Global Career Accelerator (The Accelerator), have significantly higher college retention rates than peers who did not participate.

The Accelerator is a for-credit academic initiative that offers students work-integrated learning within their college curriculum. The Accelerator aims to boost career readiness for students by rotating participants through immersive projects and live experiences co-designed with Podium's 50-plus industry partners, including Crocs, L'Oreal, and Wells Fargo.

Through an innovative student success research partnership between Podium, the University of California, Irvine, and Arizona State University (ASU), UC Irvine researchers tracked over 350,000 ASU students across three academic cohorts from 2021-2022 through 2023-2024. The findings show that students who completed Podium's Accelerator remained enrolled in subsequent semesters at rates 6 to 10 percentage points higher than non-participants year over year.

In a matched-sample analysis, which paired nearly 3,000 participants with demographically and academically similar peers, participants were retained at 90%, compared to 86% for matched non-participants. Additionally, researchers found statistically significant improvements in retention after controlling for factors like first-generation status, Pell eligibility, online versus on-campus enrollment, race, and GPA.

"The consistency of this finding across three years and two distinct analytic methods points to the exciting results of this experiential programming," said Richard Arum, Professor of Sociology and Education at UC Irvine.

"The results of this study are promising," said Anne Jones, ASU vice provost for undergraduate education. "The ASU Global Career Accelerator helps students see how their academic experience connects to the world of work. That kind of relevance can be powerful in keeping students engaged and on track to complete their degree."

Podium's innovative platform is available to more than 1.7 million students, including over 550,000 who are Pell-eligible, across more than 100 university partners. The program is backed by leading industry partners ranging from large technology organizations like Intel to consumer brands like Procter & Gamble, to non-profits like charity: water.

Increasing demand for work-integrated college experiences is driving Podium's growth. Recent data from the Business-Higher Education Forum reports that the gap between internship interest among college students and availability is a growing concern. While 8.2M learners in the U.S. reported wanting one annually, only an estimated 2.5M high-quality internships are available.

The Accelerator was designed to close that gap by embedding real, credit-bearing work experience directly into the degree, with no prerequisites, so access doesn't depend on a student's major, financial means, or ability to relocate.

"This research is the first large-scale, independent confirmation of what we've seen anecdotally since day one — that when students get real, embedded work experience, they see a brighter future for themselves and stay in college," said Chris Parrish, Co-Founder and President at Podium Education. "We're committed to expanding our partnerships with institutions to offer more industry-integrated academic experiences to both drive stronger retention for schools and better return on investment for students."

About the Research

UC Irvine researchers Richard Arum and Jeffrey M. DeVries independently conducted and reported the study, in collaboration with Jennifer Malerich of Arizona State University, and the UC Irvine Institutional Review Board reviewed and approved it. The UC Irvine research team maintained full analytic independence throughout.

A full accounting of methodology, including cohort-specific and propensity-score-matched models, is available to download: HERE.

About Podium Education

Podium Education is the leading experiential education company partnering with universities and industry to embed scalable, real-world, high-impact practices directly into the undergraduate degree for credit. Podium works with more than 100 universities, including ASU, Penn State, and Rice, and 50+ leading industry partners like L'Oréal, OpenAI, and Wells Fargo. Podium's experiences deliver fully digital, for-credit learning that strengthens student retention, confidence, and career readiness. Students from all backgrounds gain early career experience, explore potential pathways, and build the skills and competencies employers expect through hands-on, work-based learning experiences aligned with workforce needs. For more information, visit Podium Education at www.podiumeducation.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

releases.body:
Career services teams nationwide can now use RippleMatch's career guidance, opportunities marketplace and job search analytics tools at no cost.

BOSTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RippleMatch, a leading early career recruiting platform, today announced that its university product is now available free of charge to all higher education institutions. The news follows RippleMatch's acquisition by JobGet, the fastest-growing job platform connecting workers to employers at scale, and provides universities a valuable tool to support students through an entry-level hiring market that's challenged by AI disruption.

"Career services teams are being asked to do more for students at exactly the moment when the job market has become most unpredictable for them," said Audrey Patenaude, General Manager of RippleMatch. "AI is reshaping the entry-level roles where graduates have traditionally gotten their start. The job search process has become more opaque, and universities are doing this with fewer resources than ever. With our acquisition by JobGet, we've gained access to a dramatically larger job inventory and employer network, and that growth allows us to expand access to universities at no cost, and we believe that's what this moment calls for."

The announcement comes as recent graduates face one of the toughest labor markets in years. Unemployment among recent college graduates has climbed to 5.7% — a three-year high — while underemployment sits at 41.5%. Junior-level job postings fell 7% last year even as senior-level openings grew, and AI is reshaping the career ladder.

Universities are absorbing this pressure directly. Higher education institutions shed over 9,000 positions in 2025, and budget constraints have left many career services teams trying to support more students with fewer resources.

RippleMatch's Free Platform for University Career Centers

Through RippleMatch, students gain access to a personalized job feed matched to their skills and goals, verified skill badges recognized by employers, and an application process that surfaces them directly to recruiters, resulting in interview rates 20x higher than traditional job boards.

For career services teams, the platform provides real-time analytics on student engagement, verified skills, application volume, interview conversion rates, and placement outcomes, as well as tools to communicate directly with student cohorts and track activity across communities.

The acquisition of RippleMatch by JobGet further expands the diversity and volume of job opportunities available to students on the platform, adding JobGet's broad employer network to RippleMatch's existing early career recruiting relationships.

RippleMatch's university platform is available immediately to all higher education institutions at no cost. Universities can get started at ripplematch.com/universities.

About RippleMatch

RippleMatch is an early career recruiting platform that connects students with employers through intelligent matching, verified skills assessments, and personalized job feeds. Trusted by universities and employers across the country, RippleMatch is now part of the JobGet family of products.

About JobGet

JobGet is the leading hourly hiring platform helping employers and workers connect faster across the U.S. With a reach of over 100 million job seekers, JobGet combines large-scale candidate supply, AI-powered screening, interview scheduling, and hiring manager workflows to help employers hire more efficiently. JobGet partners with leading brands including Whole Foods, Avis, Hobby Lobby, Sprouts, Taco Bell, Uber, Aldi, UPS, and more to fill everyday roles across food service, retail, customer service, hospitality, manufacturing, construction, healthcare, warehouse, transportation, and other high-volume hiring categories. Through its acquisition of RippleMatch, JobGet is expanding its reach into early career and university recruiting.

Notes to Editors

On graduate unemployment and underemployment: 5.7% unemployment rate among recent college graduates (Q4 2025, three-year high) and 41.5% underemployment rate. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Labor Market for Recent College Graduates, newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market; Economic Policy Institute, Class of 2026, epi.org.

On junior-level job postings: 7% year-over-year decline in junior-level postings. Source: CNBC, New College Graduates Face a Tough Job Market (April 2026), cnbc.com.

On higher education job losses: Over 9,000 positions eliminated across higher education institutions in 2025. Source: Inside Higher Ed, December Cuts Close Out Brutal Year for Sector (January 2026), insidehighered.com.

Peer-reviewed article by University of Phoenix scholars identifies curriculum-career alignment, critical thinking, and experiential learning and mentorship as strategies graduates associate with career readiness.

PHOENIX, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies scholars affiliated with the Center for Educational and Instructional Technology Research (CEITR) have published a peer-reviewed study examining how higher education institutions can support graduate employability as workplace skill demands continue to change.
releases.title: Graduate employability study finds career-connected learning and real-world experience are priorities for college graduates
releases.body:
Peer-reviewed article by University of Phoenix scholars identifies curriculum-career alignment, critical thinking, and experiential learning and mentorship as strategies graduates associate with career readiness.

PHOENIX, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies scholars affiliated with the Center for Educational and Instructional Technology Research (CEITR) have published a peer-reviewed study examining how higher education institutions can support graduate employability as workplace skill demands continue to change.

Published in the International Journal of Innovative Business Strategies, as the article, "Graduate Employability in a Changing World," the mixed-methods study draws on the perspectives of 380 graduates of U.S. colleges and universities and found strong agreement that employability is supported when academic learning is intentionally connected to careers, practical applications and opportunities to develop adaptable skills.

Among 11 employability strategies evaluated by respondents, connecting curriculum to careers received the highest rating, followed by teaching critical thinking and adaptability, incorporating real-world applications and encouraging internships or employment. The researchers found that graduates especially associated employability development with practices delivered through faculty instruction, advising and mentoring.

"Our findings suggest graduates value career relevance when it is built throughout the educational experience," said Rheanna Reed, DM, lead author and research fellow in the Center for Educational and Instructional Technology Research (CEITR) at University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies. "Connecting learning to careers, creating opportunities to apply knowledge and helping learners develop adaptability can make career readiness a more intentional part of higher education."

Graduates emphasize experiential learning and practical skill development

Open-ended responses reinforced the quantitative findings. Among 306 graduates responding to a question about employability best practices, experiential learning was the most frequently cited strategy, appearing in 77 responses. Other frequently identified practices included skill development, mentorship and networking, and curriculum-career alignment.

The study also identified barriers that may make employability opportunities harder to access. Among 292 respondents answering a question about challenges, time constraints and competing responsibilities were cited most frequently. Labor market and financial constraints were also identified.

The researchers conclude that higher education institutions can support employability by integrating career relevance across curricula, expanding access to experiential learning, strengthening mentoring and networking opportunities, and encouraging self-directed learning and continuous skill development.

The authors note that the study reflects graduates' self-reported perceptions and does not directly measure the effectiveness of particular institutional practices or establish causal relationships. Its cross-sectional design and panel-based sample also limit the extent to which findings can be generalized.

The authors previously presented study findings in a session titled, "Graduate career readiness and employability: Global issues in education and research," at the London International Conference on Education, November 3-5, 2025, and at the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies' Knowledge Without Boundaries Summit in October 2025.

About the authors

The authors are affiliates of the Center for Educational and Instructional Technology Research (CEITR), housed within the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies, which supports scholarly research and collaboration on topics related to teaching and learning, online and in-person education, educational technology strategies, and educational policies, practices and theories.

Rheanna Reed, DM, is a research fellow with the CEITR and serves as Faculty Quality Assurance Manager at the University. She has worked in higher education since 2006 and conducts research focused on instructional quality, faculty support, student success and graduate employability. She earned her Doctor of Management in Organizational Leadership from University of Phoenix.

Louise Underdahl, Ph.D. is a doctoral instructor in the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies and a research fellow with CEITR. Her scholarship examines graduate employability, career development, mentorship, worker autonomy and human-AI collaboration. Underdahl has taught at University of Phoenix since 2004 and earned her doctorate from the University of Southern California.

Nicole Gulley, Ed.D., is a University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies alumna affiliated with CEITR. Her research interests include student retention and graduate employability, and she has contributed to University research examining nontraditional online student retention as well as employer needs, graduate skills and curriculum design.

Shawishi Haynes, Ph.D., Ed.D., serves as a University Research Methodologist in the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies and is affiliated with CEITR. Haynes has more than 30 years of healthcare leadership experience and has been faculty at University of Phoenix since 2008, serving in multiple academic and leadership capacities. Her research interests include graduate employability, student retention, healthcare workforce challenges, and alignment between academic preparation and evolving workforce needs.

Mar Navarro, Ph.D., is a University Research Methodologist in the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies and a CEITR research fellow. Her research focuses on cognition and cognitive ergonomics, including how people learn, understand and process information, with particular interests in online teaching and learning, student retention and graduate employability.

The full article, "Graduate Employability in a Changing World," is available in the International Journal of Innovative Business Strategies, 11(1), at https://infonomics-society.org/ijibs/published-papers/volume-11-2025/.

About the College of Doctoral Studies

TULSA, Okla., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Alliance Resource Partners, L.P. Visit www.CoalBenefits.com/scholars-winners to see student photos. The company also announced the teachers chosen by the top-ranked students to receive Teacher Achievement Awards.

releases.title: Sargento Welcomes Back to College Season with Forbes Award: Named One of America's Best Employers for New Grads 2026
releases.body:
The family-owned company marks the fall semester with national honor celebrating its culture of growth and development for early-career professionals.

PLYMOUTH, Wis., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As college students head back to campus for the fall semester, Sargento is proud to announce it has been named by Forbes as one of America's Best Employers for New Grads 2026. This prestigious accolade highlights the family-owned company's dedication to fostering a workplace where recent graduates can thrive, grow, and make a meaningful impact from day one.

The Forbes ranking was determined through an independent survey of over 100,000 U.S. young professionals (under 10 years of experience) working at companies employing at least 1,000 people. Out of 2 million evaluations, scores were based on direct employee nominations and public recommendations from industry peers.

The recognition marks the second major Forbes honor for Sargento in 2026. Earlier this year, Sargento was named to the Forbes list of America's Best Midsize Employers, solidifying its reputation as an employer of choice across all career stages.

"Our success has always been driven by our employees: the Sargento Family. We are committed to welcoming new graduates and students into our workforce, where they contribute at a high level and bring new ideas and ways of working to Sargento," said Louie Gentine, third-generation Chairman and CEO of Sargento. "Being recognized by Forbes as a top employer for both new graduates and midsize companies in America is an incredible honor. It shows that the culture we have built over generations continues to drive our success and makes Sargento a place where you can start and grow your career."

2026 Survey Highlights Strong Talent Pipeline   

Sargento's recognition is reinforced by the standout results of its 2026 Intern-Co-Op Survey*, which evaluated program performance, environment, and development:

  • 100% Program Advocacy: 100% of respondents stated they would recommend the Sargento internship or co-op experience to others.
  • 100% Fair Compensation Perception: 100% of participants agreed they are paid fairly for their work and contributions.
  • High Career Intent: 95% of interns and co-ops expressed a desire to accept a full-time, entry-level opportunity with Sargento upon graduation.
  • Exceptional Overall Quality: 95% rated their overall internship experience positively, supported by high marks for program leadership (100%), onboarding (91%), and skill-building projects (91%).

*The 2026 Intern-Co-Op Survey included 21 interns and co-ops, with a 100% participation rate.

"We don't view our interns and co-ops as temporary team members. We view them as the future of our business," said Anne Troka, Senior Manager of Community and Workforce Development at Sargento. "Seeing 95% of our 2026 cohort express a desire to stay with us full-time, alongside a 100% recommendation rating, proves that our focus on structured mentorship and high-impact work is creating a meaningful launchpad for early careers."

Sargento's Workforce Development program, which spans 21 distinct internship tracks across the organization, launched in 2016. Over the past decade, Sargento has established itself as an industry leader in connecting students to careers and transforming new graduates into long-term employees.

In 2026, the company welcomed its 50th student employee into a full-time role since 2016. The longevity of this program is reflected in its people. One of Sargento's earliest student hires from 2017 remains with the company today, with many of these employees choosing to grow their careers at Sargento for five years or more.

That focus on mentorship and real-world responsibility resonates with program participants.

"The most meaningful part of my internship was being surrounded by incredible mentors who encouraged my growth while trusting me with projects that allowed me to make real impact," said Carter Parker, Consumer Insights Intern, University of Michigan.

Looking ahead to the next class of leaders, applications are now open for 2027 internship and co-op programs at Sargento. To explore early-career opportunities, visit: careers.sargento.com/us/en/students

To discover how the family culture at Sargento drives meaningful impact for its people and communities, view the 2025 Impact Report here: https://www.sargentofoods.com/our-stories/real-impact-report/

About Sargento

With over 2,500 employees and $1.7 billion in net sales, Sargento is a family-owned company that has been a leader in cheese for more than 70 years. Founded in 1953 in Plymouth, Wisconsin, Sargento is proud to be the company that successfully introduced America to pre-packaged sliced and shredded natural cheeses and cheese blends. Today, Sargento is still based in Wisconsin, where they manufacture and market amazing shredded, sliced and snack natural cheese products, as well as ingredients. Company leadership lives to serve local communities and employees, whom they refer to as the Sargento Family. www.sargento.com

releases.title: College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free
releases.body:
Early College students can earn an associate degree while still in high school, potentially saving families tens of thousands of dollars.

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "I couldn't imagine how much money worth of free education my kids have received through this program."

For Ciara Selden-Ruffin, the mother of Grand River Preparatory High School Early College student Aamir Hollowell, the financial impact of the Early College program has been substantial. It has given Aamir the opportunity to earn an associate degree without the family taking on the tuition bill.

That kind of financial head start is critical for families worrying about how they will pay for college.

The nation's federal student loan portfolio stands at nearly $1.7 trillion, with about 44.6 million borrowers carrying federal education debt. The issue is back in the national spotlight as changes to the Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, Plan ended, requiring millions of borrowers to find a new way to repay their federal student loans.

For families with children approaching college, the uncertainty underscores a different question: What if students could reduce or even avoid some college debt before graduating from high school?

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) Early College program is helping their students do exactly that.

A $67,000 Head Start

At Grand River Prep, an NHA partner-school in Grand Rapids, Mich., students can earn college credits, career credentials, and even an associate degree through the school's Early College partnership with Davenport University.

Tuition, fees, and books are covered through the program. Based on Davenport's current published undergraduate tuition rate, the value of a two-year associate degree can total approximately $67,000.

Felicia Pope, who works with Davenport University's Early College partnerships, said the program can put students in a very different financial position when they enter adulthood.

"You can be 18, 19 years old, you have an associate degree, you have the entry-level position in the field, without any student loans," Pope said.

Students can use that degree to begin working in their chosen field or continue toward a bachelor's degree with a significant amount of college coursework already completed. "You're halfway through your degree, saved a ton of time, a ton of money," Pope said.

Nine of NHA's high schools have an Early College program. During the 2024-25 school year, 565 students earned 5,186 college credits, saving an estimated $1.12 million in college tuition.

For NHA, the opportunity is about making college more accessible while preparing students for what comes next.

Koree Woodward, NHA Director of High Schools, says Early College is a natural extension of NHA's mission to prepare students for life after graduation.

"The program makes college feel more attainable for families who may not have otherwise seen it as an accessible option," Woodward said. "It helps students develop the knowledge, habits, character, and sense of responsibility needed for lifelong learning, college success, and meaningful careers."

College With a Support System

The financial savings are only part of the Early College model.

Students gradually transition into college-level work, beginning with one college course per semester during 10th grade before increasing their coursework in their junior and senior years.

Pope calls it a "soft launch into college."

Davenport advisors work directly with students on applications, degree pathways, scheduling, and course selection. Grand River Prep advisors provide another layer of support, helping students monitor grades, manage college expectations, and stay on track.

Aamir Hollowell sees that support firsthand.

"Every week, you have a meeting with your advisor to help you stay on track," she said. "They just keep checking up on you."

Grand River Prep Early College Advisor Jayme McWain said students get the independence of college without having to navigate the experience alone.

"For them to have kind of a safety net and a support system built in is a really great feature of that program," McWain said. "It creates so much more access and skill building."

From College Credit to Career

In addition to the tuition savings, students can leave high school with college experience, career opportunities, and potentially two years of college already completed.

For some students, that head start can translate directly into a career.

Grand River Prep graduate Kennah Kalele earned an associate degree in medical assisting through Early College and is now pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Nursing at Grand Valley State University.

"I don't have to take any gen eds in the college that I'm going to, and I'm even ahead in some aspects of my nursing degree," Kalele said.

Her associate degree also helped her begin gaining professional experience. Kalele works part time as a medical transport technician while continuing her education.

For McWain, the value is clear.

"Anytime you can help someone get free college when the price is off the charts, that's a great thing," she said.

And for families like Ciara Selden-Ruffin's, it offers the opportunity for her children to start their futures with a college education rather than a tuition bill.

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) was founded in 1995 with families in mind and the belief that every child deserves an education that builds knowledge and character. Today, NHA supports 105 tuition-free, partner-schools across nine states, serving more than 65,000 K-12 students through rigorous academics and Moral Focus™ programming. NHA

releases.title: Red Bank Catholic High School and Conscientia Health Open New Wellness Room, Marking Expanded Commitment to Student Mental and Physical Health
releases.body:
Ribbon-cutting held on World Suicide Prevention Day

RED BANK, N.J., Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Red Bank Catholic High School officially opened a new Wellness Room on its Broad Street campus today, with a ribbon-cutting and blessing ceremony marking the next chapter of the school's student wellness initiative, developed in partnership with Conscientia Health. 

The event fell on World Suicide Prevention Day, within National Suicide Prevention Awareness Month, timing both organizations say reflects their shared commitment to student mental health. 

The Wellness Room is part of a broader initiative between RBC and Conscientia Health that includes a wellness curriculum focused on mental health awareness, resilience, and coping strategies; educational programming workshops; and expanded support pathways for students and families. 

"This is about creating a culture where wellness is foundational to student success," said Nicole Wall, RBC Student Assistance Counselor. "As RBC continues to expand opportunities and strengthen student support systems, we remain committed to exceeding the needs of the whole child academically, spiritually, and emotionally." 

"We didn't choose today's date, the timing found us," said Dr. Simbiat Adighije (Dr. Sim), Founder of Conscientia Health, who has led the partnership. "But it's a reminder of why this work matters. Too many young people carry real struggles quietly, and too many adults around them don't know until it's a crisis. This room is one answer to that: a place where a student can be seen and supported before things reach that point. We're proud to build that alongside Red Bank Catholic." 

The Wellness Room includes a private consultation space, a group and workshop area for peer support sessions, and a self-guided check-in tool connecting students directly with a clinician when needed. The initiative is part of RISE by Conscientia, a program extending Conscientia's integrated care model into school communities. 

About Red Bank Catholic High School 

Red Bank Catholic is a vibrant, beloved, Catholic co-educational institution with a storied history, an extraordinary spirit, and a record of achievement in the classroom and beyond. Our programs pursue excellence in faith, academics, cultural awareness, athletics, and personal wellness in a mission to fully engage the minds, hearts, and souls of students in our Roman Catholic community so that they can succeed in every aspect of their lives. 

About Conscientia Health 

Conscientia Health is a telehealth provider offering integrated psychiatry, therapy, and primary care, with a mission to make whole-person care accessible and coordinated. Conscientia operates over 20 physical locations across New Jersey, providing hybrid in-person and virtual care. 

Conscientia Health's R.I.S.E. Teen Mental Health Program supports adolescents ages 12 to 19 through personalized teen mental health services for emotional, behavioral, and mental health challenges. We help teenagers reclaim their inner strength, develop practical life skills, and build resilience through integrated behavioral health and primary care support.

releases.title: MIT POLICE ASSOCIATION DENOUNCES UNIVERSITY'S 0% RAISE OFFER FOR OFFICERS
releases.body:
University executives receive average raises of 16.7% in 2025, while police are offered 0% in three ‑ year contract proposal

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As thousands of MIT students return to campus this week—many living away from home for the first time—their families trust that MIT will keep them safe. The Institute proudly promotes its commitment to public safety, highlighting a Community Campus Safety Council, a fully staffed police department, EMT services, campus patrols, shuttle operations, and blue‑light emergency phones across campus. MIT markets safety as a cornerstone of the student experience.

But when it comes to negotiating a fair contract for the officers who provide that safety, the story is starkly different.

MIT Executive VP, Glen Shor, Police Chief John DiFava, and the university's negotiating committee have presented the MIT Police Association with a proposal that demonstrates a clear lack of respect for the men and women who protect the MIT community every day. The university is demanding that officers accept 0% in the first year of a proposed three‑year contract—while offering no guaranteed wage increases in years two and three.

Meanwhile, MIT's top executives received raises averaging 16.7%, more than quadruple the average cost‑of‑living increase.*  Chief DiFava has led MIT Police since 2001 and MIT must publicly disclose the Chiefs current compensation and whether he, too, is being asked to accept a 0% increase, and what increase did he receive in 2025.

MIT Police officers work around the clock to safeguard one of the world's most prestigious institutions. They respond to medical emergencies, protect students and faculty, investigate incidents, enforce the law, and routinely place themselves in challenging and dangerous situations. Their work is essential to the functioning of the campus. They also serve as a valued resource for the overall safety of those who live, work and visit Cambridge and Boston.

Yet MIT's message to its police officers during negotiations appears to be: Take zero now, and hope for something later.

This position is not only disrespectful—it is indefensible. MIT has the financial capacity to fairly compensate its police officers. The Institute's endowment reached $27.4 billion, buoyed by a 14.8% investment return in FY 2025. MIT's resources are vast; its refusal to invest in the safety personnel who protect its community is a choice.

MIT officers show up every day to protect students, faculty, staff, and visitors. They respond to crises, support students in vulnerable moments, and keep the campus safe 24/7. Offering officers a 0% raise while executives receive double‑digit increases sends a clear message about whose work MIT values—and whose it does not. The MIT community deserves better.

The MIT Police Association urges MIT leadership to return to the bargaining table with a fair and respectful offer that reflects the critical role officers play in keeping the campus safe.

The MIT Police Association represents about 42 patrol officers that work in the MIT Police Department.

releases.title: Pledge 1% Appoints Josh Jarrett as Chief Executive Officer
releases.body:
Technology and social impact leader will guide the global movement into its next phase of growth and impact

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pledge 1%, the global movement inspiring companies to embed social impact into their business, today announced the appointment of Josh Jarrett as Chief Executive Officer, effective September 8, 2026.

Jarrett brings nearly three decades of experience at the intersection of technology and impact, spanning philanthropy, startups, and global organizations. He helped build the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's higher education initiative, co-founded Koru and InStride to expand access to education and careers, and most recently led Wiley's Applied Research Intelligence business, where he developed AI-powered products built on trusted research.

He joins Pledge 1% at an important moment for both the organization and corporate impact. More than a decade after its founding, Pledge 1% has grown to a global community of more than 20,000 companies across 130 countries. At the same time, rapid advances in AI are reshaping business, creating new questions about how companies contribute to society and how corporate impact will evolve alongside them.

"Josh is a strong leader with experience across philanthropy, startups, and established businesses," said Scott Farquhar, Board Chair of Pledge 1%. "His work at the forefront of applied AI is particularly relevant as AI transforms our membership base. Josh has the skills to build on Pledge 1%'s incredible foundation, evolve it for a new generation of companies, and grow the movement globally."

"We're at an inflection point with the explosion of AI and fundamental questions about who will benefit from the value it creates," said Josh Jarrett, incoming CEO of Pledge 1%. "That's what makes the opportunity at Pledge 1% so compelling to me. Companies have a huge impact on our society — creating opportunity and shaping our quality of life. I'm excited about what's possible when we work with companies to expand the ways their success can benefit society more broadly."

Pledge 1% began with a simple idea and framework: make giving back part of how companies do business by committing a portion of their time, profit, product, or equity. More than a decade later, the ways companies create impact continue to evolve, along with the expectations placed on business. But the core conviction behind Pledge 1% remains the same: companies can be a powerful platform for positive impact, and that impact is strongest when it is embedded into how they do business.

About Pledge 1%: Pledge 1% is a global movement to embed social impact into all businesses. Providing a simple, flexible framework for setting aside staff time, product, profit, and/or equity, Pledge 1% is on a mission to inspire, educate, and empower companies of all sizes to leverage their assets to create positive impact and meaningful change. Over the past decade, more than 20,000 companies in more than 130 countries have joined the movement, including top industry leaders like Salesforce, Atlassian, Twilio, Airbnb, Okta, Toast, Reddit, Canva, and many more, unlocking over $3 billion of new philanthropy in equity commitments alone.

releases.title: Dr. Sergio Sokol Scholarship Launching for US Medical Students
releases.body:
NEW YORK, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Dr. Sergio Sokol Scholarship for Future Doctors officially opens its national application process, inviting aspiring physicians from across the country to apply for higher education support. Created by Dr. Sergio Sokol, a board-certified cardiologist based in New York City, the program provides funding to dedicated undergraduate, graduate, and medical students who demonstrate academic commitment, integrity, and a passion for community healthcare service.

To qualify, applicants must be current undergraduate, graduate, or medical students, or graduating high school seniors accepted into an accredited post-secondary institution. Candidates must intend to pursue a career as a physician or doctor of medicine and remain in good academic standing. Selection relies on academic dedication and an original essay submission.

Applicants must write an original essay responding to the following prompt:

"What inspires you to become a physician, and how do you hope to improve the lives of your future patients and the communities you will serve?"

The selection committee evaluates responses based on narrative clarity, personal motivation, and alignment with core clinical values, including empathy, perseverance, leadership, and public service.

Dr. Sergio Sokol established this program to encourage future healthcare leaders who embody both scientific rigor and compassionate care. Throughout his career in cardiovascular medicine, Dr. Sergio Sokol has emphasized pairing technical expertise with strong ethical values. By aiding the next generation of doctors, Dr. Sergio Sokol helps ease educational costs for candidates striving to improve patient outcomes.

Applications must be emailed to apply@drsergiosokolscholarship.com alongside proof of current enrollment or acceptance. The deadline for all materials is April 15, 2027. Following evaluation by the selection committee, the selected recipient receives a one-time award of $1,000, with the official winner announcement taking place on May 15, 2027.

Interested students can review full application guidelines and eligibility requirements by visiting the program website at https://www.drsergiosokolscholarship.com/.

About Dr. Sergio Sokol Scholarship for Future Doctors

Founded by board-certified cardiologist Dr. Sergio Sokol, the Dr. Sergio Sokol Scholarship for Future Doctors is an educational initiative dedicated to supporting aspiring physicians across the United States. The organization aims to foster academic excellence, compassionate care, and integrity among students preparing for medical careers.

releases.title: Starwood Capital Group Announces Joint Venture with Trinitas Ventures
releases.body:
Partnership to accelerate the development of three high-quality, purpose-built student housing on several of the most prominent university campuses across the United States

MIAMI and CARMEL, Ind., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Starwood Capital Group ("Starwood"), a leading global private investment firm, and Trinitas Ventures ("Trinitas"), a fully integrated real estate firm specializing in the investment, development, construction, and management of high-quality residential communities, have formed a joint venture ("the Partnership") to develop purpose-built student housing at three leading universities across the United States. The partnership combines Starwood's institutional capital and investment expertise with Trinitas' proven ability to identify, capitalize, develop, construct, and manage institutional-quality student housing communities. Together, the firms are well positioned to deliver modern, well-located communities in university markets where student housing supply has not kept pace with enrollment growth.

The Partnership has closed on three sites – Atmosphere Pittsburgh, Atmosphere Norman, and Atmosphere on Mifflin – representing a combined 2,046 beds serving the University of Pittsburgh, University of Oklahoma, and University of Wisconsin-Madison. Each community is located adjacent to leading university campuses in markets supported by strong enrollment trends and constrained purpose-built student housing supply. All three communities are targeted for delivery in Summer 2028.

Atmosphere Pittsburgh, located at 217 Halket Street in Pittsburgh's Oakland neighborhood, will deliver 672 beds across 326 units and more than 30,000 square feet of clubhouse and amenity space. Assembled across 12 parcels, the site sits adjacent to the University of Pittsburgh's core campus and within walking distance of Carnegie Mellon University and three UPMC hospitals. The University of Pittsburgh continues to grow enrollment — its 2025 freshman class expanded by 1,274 students — while the market's purpose-built beds-to-enrollment ratio remains just 8 percent.

Atmosphere Norman, located at 310 E. Boyd Street in Norman, Oklahoma, will deliver 677 beds and more than 13,700 square feet of state-of-the-art amenity space. It is the first new institutional student housing community developed pedestrian to the University of Oklahoma campus in more than a decade. OU's Norman campus enrolled a record 32,662 students in fall 2025 — its fifth consecutive year of record enrollment — even as on-campus housing waitlists have grown sharply.

Atmosphere on Mifflin, located at 619 W. Mifflin Street in Madison, Wisconsin, will deliver 697 beds across 264 units and more than 15,000 square feet of clubhouse and amenity space adjacent to the University of Wisconsin–Madison campus. The development will incorporate the historic 32-bed Wiedenbeck Apartments alongside new purpose-built residences, expanding the range of housing choices available within the community. UW–Madison's total enrollment has grown 2.6 percent annually since 2020, while the market's off-campus purpose-built beds-to-enrollment ratio remains just 18 percent, reinforcing continued demand for student housing near campus.

"Student housing at leading universities offers durable, needs-based demand and attractive risk-adjusted returns, particularly in markets where new supply has failed to keep pace with enrollment growth," said Qahir Madhany, Managing Director & Head of Acquisitions, Americas, at Starwood. "This partnership allows us to deploy capital at scale behind high-quality communities in compelling markets. We look forward to delivering these projects with Trinitas."

"This partnership pairs our fully integrated development platform with a world-class capital partner, creating an opportunity to bring high-quality communities to three of the country's strongest university markets," said Loren King, CEO and co-Founder of Trinitas Ventures. "Pittsburgh, Norman and Madison demonstrate the kind of opportunities our platform is designed to pursue. By combining disciplined market selection, deep local insight, and integrated execution across every stage of development, we're well positioned to deliver communities that elevate the student experience and reflect our core purpose of enhancing lives by creating exceptional real estate."

Newmark's student housing team, led by Executive Vice Chairman, Ryan Lang, arranged the joint venture between Trinitas and Starwood.

About Starwood Capital Group

Starwood Capital Group is a private investment firm with a core focus on real assets globally. Since its inception in 1991, Starwood Capital Group has raised over $95 billion of capital and currently has ~$130 billion of assets under management. Through a series of comingled opportunity funds and Starwood Real Estate Income Trust, Inc. (SREIT), a non-listed REIT, the Firm has invested in virtually every category of real estate on a global basis, opportunistically shifting asset classes, geographies and positions in the capital stack as it perceives risk/reward dynamics to be evolving. In July 2026, Starwood held the final closing of Starwood Distressed Opportunity Fund XIII (SOF XIII), its latest opportunistic real estate fund, with capital commitments in excess of $10.2 billion from more than 300 investors across approximately 20 countries.

Starwood Capital also manages Starwood Property Trust (NYSE: STWD), the largest commercial mortgage real estate investment trust in the United States, which has successfully deployed over $117 billion of capital since inception and manages a portfolio of over $31 billion across debt and equity investments. Alongside Starwood Property Trust, Starwood Capital manages over $6 billion in several private debt funds investing across the globe.

Starwood Capital's other affiliates include: Highmark Residential, a property management company; Starwood Digital Ventures, a platform dedicated to the firm's data center investment strategy; Starwood Hotels, a hotel brand management team; Essex Title, a title agent for one or more underwriters in issuing title policies and/or providing support services; and Starwood Oil & Gas, which seeks to capitalize on conventional and unconventional North American assets.

Additional information can be found at www.starwoodcapital.com, www.starwoodnav.reit, www.starwoodpropertytrust.com and www.starwoodhotels.com.

About Trinitas Ventures

Trinitas Ventures is a Carmel, Indiana-based fully integrated real estate firm specializing in the investment, development, construction, management, and acquisition of high-quality residential communities. For every investment, Trinitas combines data-powered foresight, institutional discipline, entrepreneurial agility, collaborative partnerships, and purpose-driven values to deliver communities that enhance lives and create lasting value. The company has developed nearly $3 billion in residential communities nationwide, with a current pipeline of projects valued at over $1 billion. Learn more at www.trinitas.ventures.

About Newmark

Newmark Group, Inc., together with its subsidiaries ("Newmark"), is a world leader in commercial real estate, seamlessly powering every phase of the property life cycle. Newmark's comprehensive suite of services and products is uniquely tailored to each client, from owners to occupiers, investors to founders, and startups to blue-chip companies. Combining the platform's global reach with market intelligence in both established and emerging property markets, Newmark provides superior service to clients across the industry spectrum. For the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, Newmark generated revenues of more than $3.4 billion. As of March 31, 2026, Newmark and its business partners together operated from over 185 offices with more than 9,600 professionals across four continents. Students can understand key information, work across languages, compare documents, and refine content as their needs shift from the classroom to campus activities and career opportunities.

Get More from Notes and Study Materials

As course materials accumulate, finding and reviewing important information can become time-consuming. Students can scan textbooks, handouts, and handwritten notes with CamScanner and use OCR, with recognition for 41 languages, to make the content searchable. With CS AI, Summarize a document can help condense lengthy materials, while Extract key details can highlight relevant information for review.

Stay on Top of Campus Activities

Club fairs and student organizations bring a steady stream of flyers, schedules, sign-up sheets, and event materials. Instead of letting this information disappear into backpacks or camera rolls, students can digitize it with CamScanner. With CS AI, Extract key details can help students identify event times, locations, and deadlines, making campus materials easier to act on.
